name: Turati's Boubou
rangeDescription: Rainforest of guinea-bissau, western guinea, and western sierra leone
description: Chunky black-and-white bushshrike. The upperparts are cleanly black and the underparts are white with a pinkish wash, especially on the breast.

name: Guatemalan Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Highlands of southern mexico (chiapas), guatemala and western el salvador
description: Small, drab tyrannulet found in the highlands of southern Mexico, Guatemala, and western El Salvador. Fairly inconspicuous; usually found as singles or pairs in middle to upper levels of forests, plantations, and second-growth.

name: Mountain Plover
rangeDescription: Great plains of western canada to southwestern usa; winters to northern mexico
description: Medium-sized, plain buffy plover that favors flat open areas with little or no vegetation. Plain whitish underparts with no breast band.

name: Biak Paradise-Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Biak (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: A fairly common, long-tailed kingfisher of primary and degraded forest on Biak Island where it is the only paradise-kingfisher. White underparts, rump and long tail with large spatules, thick red bill, dark blue upperparts and pale blue flecked head, shoulder patch and narrow part of the tail.

name: Rufous-tailed Plantcutter
rangeDescription: Central and southern chile and argentina
description: Distinctive bird found in varied wooded and semiopen habitats, from town gardens to meadows and bogs in Andean foothills. Often seen perched on roadside wires.

name: Riparian Antbird
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia to northeastern bolivia and southwestern amazonian brazil
description: Skulky, long-tailed antbird. Males are dark gray; females are lighter grayish brown above, orange below with an orange face.

name: Thick-billed Spiderhunter
rangeDescription: Forest of peninsular thailand, malay peninsula, sumatra, and borneo
description: Dull and largely unmarked spiderhunter. Brownish olive above with a yellow belly, faint yellow crescents around the eye, and faint speckling on the crown.

name: Pantepui Thrush
rangeDescription: Southeastern venezuela (amazonas and bolívar) and guyana
description: A drab thrush, found only in tepuis. Nondescript grayish-brown with a pale whitish belly.

name: Omao
rangeDescription: Highlands of hawaii
description: A plump thrush of dense native forests above 3,000 feet elevation on the eastern side of Hawaii Island. Also occurs sparsely in high montane shrubland.

name: Dark-winged Miner
rangeDescription: Andes of central peru (western junín, huancavelica, lima, and pasco)
description: Plain bird found in treeless areas of the high Andes of central Peru. Plumage is sandy brown with a buffy tinge on the face and breast.

name: Plum-throated Cotinga
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southeastern colombia to northern bolivia and western amazonian brazil
description: Bright blue cotinga of lowland rainforest. Males are pure sky blue, with a purple throat and light eye; females are buffy tan with faint scalloping.

name: Sangihe Hanging-Parrot
rangeDescription: Sangihe islands (north of sulawesi)
description: A tiny, green, very short-tailed parrot restricted to Sangihe Island. Mostly bright green with a red rump, upper tail, and throat in both sexes.

name: Himalayan Bulbul
rangeDescription: Northeastern afghanistan and himalayas from northern pakistan eastward at least to arunachal (northeastern india)
description: Sharp-looking bulbul with a spiffy mohawk. Note black face and throat, bright white cheek spot, and yellow vent.

name: Speckled Rail
rangeDescription: Locally in lowlands of south america east of the andes
description: Very rare and poorly known, but likely widely overlooked, small rail of the southern cone from SE Brazil to central Argentina. Its secretive nature makes it difficult to understand its habitat and habits, but timing of records, combined with records from the middle of downtown Buenos Aires and São Paolo, suggest it is at least somewhat migratory.

name: White-fronted Manakin
rangeDescription: Southeastern guyana, suriname, french guiana, and northern amazonian brazil
description: An unobtrusive, sparrow-sized bird of rainforest understory. Male is glossy black with a bright blue rump, a shining white forehead, a large yellow central breast spot, and a yellow belly.

name: American Black Duck
rangeDescription: Northeastern north america; winters to bahamas and gulf coast
description: A large duck, nearly identical to Mallard in size and shape but with a much darker chocolate-colored body. Bill is yellow with a slight greenish tinge on males, dull grayish-green on females.

name: Olive-streaked Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Foothills and highlands of costa rica and western panama (to chiriquí and ngäbe-buglé)
description: Small, fruit-eating flycatcher found in lower to middle levels of humid forest. Most common in the mountains, but occasionally seen in lowland areas.

name: Red-billed Pytilia
rangeDescription: Highlands of western and central ethiopia
description: A pretty and distinctive waxbill that is mostly gray with red wings, tail, and bill. Females are slightly duller and more brownish than males.

name: Dot-backed Antbird
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia to southern venezuela, northern bolivia, and amazonian brazil
description: Fairly small, short-tailed antbird. Fairly widespread in lowland forest of the Amazon basin in northern South America, often around water.

name: Cinereous Owl
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern mexico (durango) to veracruz and oaxaca
description: Large, dark-eyed owl restricted to pine and pine-oak forests in western and central Mexico. Apparently rare and local; only known from a handful of sites.
